title: Huckleberry Hideaway
bestFor: Couples seeking an unplugged, off-grid glamping retreat
bestSeason: Summer through fall — berry season and warm outdoor showers
description:
Huckleberry Hideaway
Off-grid A-frame glamping cabin in Gold Bar, Washington
1 Bedroom · Sleeps 2
7-acre gated property near the Skykomish River
body: An off-grid A-frame cabin on a stunning 7-acre gated property in the Cascade foothills, minutes from the Wild and Scenic Skykomish River. This is glamping done right: a dreamy queen bed with sheepskin rugs, a wood-burning stove, covered front porch, and a private gas firepit area out back. There is no electricity or running water in the cabin, but you get rechargeable lights, a solar charging station, fresh drinking water, and a seasonal outdoor shower down the trail. The covered outdoor kitchen has a cookstove, cast iron pans, drip coffee maker, and basics. Wander trails lined with wild berries — huckleberries, salmonberries, thimbleberries — and watch trains roll by from the property. Rafting, rock climbing, hiking, and skiing are all minutes away. The host, Paula, lights the fire before you arrive and is known for exceptional hospitality. A true unplugged retreat for couples who want simplicity done beautifully.

title: Evergreen Cascades Dome
bestFor: Couples and hikers seeking a cozy dome basecamp near North Cascades NP
bestSeason: Late spring through fall — access to the full North Cascades
description:
Evergreen Cascades Dome
Glamping Dome in Rockport, Washington (near North Cascades NP)
1 Bedroom · 1 Bath (1 half) · Sleeps 2
$152–$401/night
body: A 400-square-foot geodesic dome tucked in the forest just off Highway 20, 11 minutes from the western entrance of North Cascades National Park. The dome itself is cozy and well-appointed: a queen bed surrounded by trees, a wood-burning fireplace, high-speed WiFi, and a private hot tub under the stars. Step outside to an outdoor kitchen with grill and mini fridge, a fire pit with ample firewood, and a hot water outdoor shower. Barr Creek trailhead and a scenic waterfall are a 5-minute walk. The property sits on 2.5 acres of forest with the Skagit River nearby. Pet-friendly, so your dog can come too. Note: Highway 20 closes seasonally for winter, but the dome is accessible year-round from the west side.

title: Timber Stilts Treehouse Cabin
bestFor: Couples or small families wanting a treehouse experience with real comfort
bestSeason: Winter — snowmobile access and a private winter wonderland
description:
Timber Stilts Treehouse Cabin
Vacation Home in Kittitas County (Roslyn), Washington
2 Bedrooms · 4 Beds · 1 Bathroom
Sleeps 6

1 hour to Leavenworth. 10 min to downtown Roslyn. 40 min to Snoqualmie Pass.
body: Everyone in the area knows the house on stilts. This 1970s cedar cabin sits high in the trees with a mid-century modern interior, a suspended vintage fireplace, and a wraparound deck that feels like living in the canopy. The owners spent years renovating this gem before opening it to guests, and it shows — every detail is intentional, from the fully stocked kitchen to the curated games and books. Soak in the hot tub under the stars, cook on the gas grill, or venture out to Cle Elum Lake, miles of dirt bike and snowmobile trails, and the historic town of Roslyn just 10 minutes away. In winter, the adventure intensifies: roads close to cars and you hike or snowmobile in, which only makes arriving feel more rewarding. One hour to Leavenworth, 1.5 hours to Seattle. No pets, no smoking, no events. Private elopements welcome.

title: Tiny Home #3 on Icicle Creek
bestFor: Small families or friends wanting creek-side access to Leavenworth adventures
bestSeason: Summer — creek swimming, hiking, and Leavenworth festivals
description:
Tiny Home #3 on Icicle Creek
Tiny home in Leavenworth, Washington
1 bedroom, 2 beds, 1 bath
Sleeps 4
body: Tucked along the banks of Icicle Creek in the shadow of the Cascades, this thoughtfully designed tiny home punches far above its footprint. Floor-to-ceiling windows frame the creek and mountain views, while the compact but clever layout gives you everything you need — full kitchen, comfortable sleeping for four, and a front-row seat to some of Washington State's best outdoor recreation. Step outside and you're minutes from Icicle Gorge trailheads, rock climbing at Peshastin Pinnacles, and the Bavarian charm of downtown Leavenworth. Part of the Icicle River RV Resort, it blends the tiny home aesthetic with resort-level reliability.

title: Ridgeline Cabin - Peaceful mountain retreat
bestFor: Couples seeking a serene mountain escape near Leavenworth
bestSeason: Fall — golden larches and crisp mountain air
description:
Ridgeline Cabin - Peaceful mountain retreat - Airbnb
Entire cabin in Leavenworth, Washington
1 bedroom · 1 king bed · 2 baths
Sleeps 2
body: Perched on a ridgeline overlooking the Cascade Mountains, this peaceful cabin retreat offers panoramic views and complete serenity just minutes from downtown Leavenworth. Hosted by Nancy, a retired RN of 40 years with an eye for detail and service, the cabin is immaculately maintained and thoughtfully appointed. Wake to mountain sunrises, soak in the hot tub under the stars, and let the silence of the Cascades reset your compass. A perfect escape for couples seeking quiet luxury in the heart of Washington wine country.

body: As we wander through the trees, the rustle of leaves and snapping of twigs beneath our feet serve as a reminder that we're about to experience something special. The Glamping Getaway in Copperhill, Tennessee, is a treehouse resort that embodies the spirit of adventure and relaxation. With four unique treehouses, each with its own character and charm, you can choose the one that suits your needs. The Rubicon, Stamish Castle, La Paz, and Dreamweaver treehouses offer a range of sleeping arrangements, from cozy studios to spacious lofts. As you settle into your treehouse, the sounds of the forest will lull you into a state of tranquility, and the wood-fired hot tub will be waiting to soothe your muscles. Whether you're looking to unwind or explore the surrounding wilderness, this treehouse resort is the perfect retreat. As you explore the resort, you'll discover a kitchen, deck, patio, and grill, all designed to make your stay comfortable and enjoyable. With its pet-friendly policy and ample parking, this resort is ideal for families, groups of friends, and couples alike.

body: As you step into the Alpine Treehouse, you're enveloped in the warmth of modern alpine luxury. This slopeside penthouse apartment in Stowe, Vermont, offers expansive views of Mt Mansfield, with the Gondola and Spruce Peak lifts just steps away. The open-concept living area, with its floor-to-ceiling windows, pristine chef's kitchen, and comfy seating, is the perfect space to unwind after a day on the slopes. body: As you step into this historic 1850 lighthouse, the weight of time settles around you. The Keweenaw Peninsula, a remote stretch of Lake Superior's shoreline, is a place where the rhythms of the past still linger. You'll find yourself drawn to the immense silence of the lake, the superior sunsets that paint the sky with hues of gold and crimson, and the simplicity of life in a fully restored lighthouse. The three bedrooms offer a cozy retreat, a place to unwind and let the sound of the waves lull you into a deep sleep.

title: Braddock Point Lighthouse
subtitle: 128-year-old Coast Guard lighthouse on Lake Ontario
bestFor: Couples and families looking for a unique, historic experience
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and calm lake waters make it ideal for swimming and boating
description: Braddock Point Lighthouse — a 128-year-old Coast Guard-maintained lighthouse on the shores of Lake Ontario outside Rochester. Three bedrooms inside the original keeper's dwelling, with the tower itself still actively guiding ships.
body: As you step into the Braddock Point Lighthouse, the weight of 128 years of history settles around you. The original keeper's dwelling, now a cozy three-bedroom abode, still stands sentinel on the shores of Lake Ontario. The tower, still actively guiding ships, is a reminder of the importance of this stretch of coastline. We imagine waking up to the sound of waves gently lapping against the shore, the scent of lake water and damp earth filling the air. The lighthouse's rugged beauty is a testament to its enduring presence, a constant in an ever-changing world. As you explore the keeper's dwelling, you'll uncover the stories of those who came before, their lives a testament to the power of the lake and the importance of this guiding light.

title: Cove Point Lighthouse Keeper's House
subtitle: Chesapeake Bay keeper's quarters at a working lighthouse
bestFor: Couples and families seeking a unique, historic experience
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and gentle breezes off the Chesapeake Bay
description: The keeper's house at Cove Point Lighthouse on the Chesapeake Bay — stay at one of Maryland's most historic lighthouses while the tower still flashes above you. Three bedrooms, Chesapeake sunsets, and living history.
body: As you step into the keeper's house at Cove Point Lighthouse, the soft creak of the old wooden floorboards beneath your feet serves as a reminder that you're walking in the footsteps of generations past. The Chesapeake Bay stretches out before you, its sunsets a kaleidoscope of pinks, oranges, and purples that seem to shift and deepen as the day wanes. With three bedrooms to settle into, this historic house is a place to slow down, to watch the tower's light slice through the darkness, and to feel the weight of history in the silence. We find ourselves drawn to the gentle rhythms of this working lighthouse, where the past and present coexist in a beautiful, seaward-facing harmony.

title: Bristol Ferry Lighthouse
subtitle: Restored 1855 lighthouse on Narragansett Bay
bestFor: Couples and solo travelers seeking a historic, peaceful retreat
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and long days to explore the town and bay
description: Bristol Ferry Lighthouse — a beautifully restored 1855 lighthouse on Narragansett Bay in Rhode Island. Water views in every direction, the classic New England lighthouse keeper's life, and the quiet dignity of a building that guided ships for over a century.
body: As you step into the Bristol Ferry Lighthouse, you're enveloped in the quiet dignity of a building that's guided ships for over a century. The classic New England lighthouse keeper's life is yours to experience, with water views in every direction and the gentle lapping of Narragansett Bay's waves against the shore. We imagine you spending your days exploring the historic town of Bristol, and your evenings watching the sunset over the bay from the lighthouse's lofty heights. The beautifully restored 1855 lighthouse is a testament to a bygone era, its historic charm and character waiting to be soaked up by those who appreciate the simple, elegant things in life.

title: Wings Neck Lighthouse
subtitle: Iconic Cape Cod lighthouse on its own private peninsula
bestFor: Families or groups of friends looking for a unique and historic stay
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and calm seas make it ideal for swimming and water activities
description: Wings Neck Lighthouse is one of the most celebrated lighthouse rentals in America — a historic 1875 tower on its own private peninsula on Buzzards Bay at Cape Cod. Four bedrooms, private beach, and stunning 360-degree water views.
body: As you step onto the private peninsula, the 1875 Wings Neck Lighthouse tower rises before you, its historic presence a reminder of the stories it holds. We've had the privilege of staying in some remarkable places, but there's something special about being surrounded by water on all sides, with the sound of the bay lapping against the shore. The four bedrooms and private beach make it an ideal setup for a group of friends or family, and the 360-degree water views are a constant reminder of the unique setting. You'll find yourself wandering the peninsula, taking in the sights and sounds of the bay, and feeling the weight of history in this special place.

title: Sitka Lighthouse — Private Luxury in Alaska
subtitle: Remote Alaskan lighthouse, Inside Passage grandeur
bestFor: Couples and families seeking solitude and a connection with nature
bestSeason: Summer — peak whale watching season
description: A private luxury lighthouse on the wild shores of Sitka, Alaska — backdropped by the snow-capped peaks of the Inside Passage. Three bedrooms, complete seclusion, and the possibility of seeing humpbacks and sea otters from your doorstep.
body: As you step into the Sitka Lighthouse, the wild shores of Alaska unfold before you like a canvas of unspoiled nature. The snow-capped peaks of the Inside Passage rise up in the distance, a constant reminder of the vast, untouched beauty that surrounds you. With three bedrooms and complete seclusion, this private luxury lighthouse is the perfect retreat for those seeking solitude and connection with the natural world. From your doorstep, you may catch a glimpse of humpbacks and sea otters, their gentle movements a soothing balm for the soul.

title: Stay in a Working Lighthouse!
subtitle: Active Pacific lighthouse, Pacific Ocean views
bestFor: Couples and solo travelers seeking a unique, historic experience
bestSeason: Winter — storm watching season, with dramatic waves and a cozy atmosphere
description: A privately owned working lighthouse on the Oregon Coast with sweeping Pacific Ocean views. Sleep in the keeper's quarters while the light still sweeps the ocean below — one of the genuinely rarest overnight stays in America.
body: As you step into the keeper's quarters of this working lighthouse in Brookings, Oregon, the sound of the Pacific Ocean waves and the occasional sweep of the light above become the constant companions of your stay. The quarters, with their historic charm, offer a unique glimpse into the life of a lighthouse keeper, while the views of the ocean unfolding below are a reminder of the importance of this beacon on the coast. We find the rhythm of the light and the sea to be hypnotic, a soothing melody that accompanies every moment of your time here.

title: Lighthouse with Hot Tub — San Juan Islands Views
subtitle: Island-dotted Pacific panoramas from your own lighthouse
bestFor: Couples seeking a romantic getaway
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and long days to enjoy the views
description: A lighthouse perched above the Salish Sea with a hot tub and sweeping views of the San Juan Islands — one of the most scenic vistas in the Pacific Northwest. Watch ferries glide between islands while the sunset turns the water gold.
body: As you step into this lighthouse, the Salish Sea unfolds before you like a canvas of blues and greens. The San Juan Islands rise up from the water, their rugged silhouettes a reminder of the wild beauty that lies just beyond the shore. You can watch the ferries glide between the islands, their gentle wake disturbing the otherwise glassy surface of the sea. As the sun sets, the water is set aflame, turning a deep gold that seems to seep into every pore of the landscape. It's a view that's both calming and exhilarating, a reminder of the power and beauty of the natural world. The hot tub, perched on the edge of the lighthouse, is the perfect place to soak up the view, the warm water a comforting contrast to the cool sea air.

title: Hobbit House of Pawling
subtitle: Hudson Valley earth home with private hot tub
bestFor: Couples seeking a romantic retreat
bestSeason: Autumn — foliage season in the Hudson Valley
description: A cozy, one-of-a-kind hobbit house in the Hudson Valley with a private hot tub — an earthen fantasy retreat two hours from Manhattan. Round doors, curved walls, and the rolling Pawling hills stretching outside.
body: As you step into the Hobbit House of Pawling, the curved walls and round doors envelop you in a sense of earthy tranquility. The rolling hills of Pawling stretch out before you, a gentle reminder of the natural world that awaits just beyond the threshold. We've found that the best way to experience this unique stay is to settle into its rhythms, letting the soft earth tones and organic shapes calm the mind and soothe the soul. The private hot tub is the perfect spot to unwind, surrounded by the soothing sounds of the Hudson Valley.

title: Luxury Hobbit House with Private Hot Tub
subtitle: Year-round earth home retreat in southern Maine
bestFor: Couples and families seeking a peaceful, natural retreat
bestSeason: Fall — the foliage season brings a kaleidoscope of colors to the surrounding woods
description: A luxurious hobbit house at Littlefield Retreat — a 15-acre woodland village on a Maine pond with treehouses and earth homes. Private hot tub, two bedrooms, and the feeling of a fairy tale that somehow also has heated floors.
body: As you step into this luxury hobbit house, the feeling of a fairy tale settles in, with heated floors and plush comforts that belie its earthy, natural surroundings. The private hot tub is a serene oasis, set amidst the 15-acre woodland village of Littlefield Retreat, where treehouses and earth homes blend seamlessly into the landscape. We find ourselves drawn to the gentle lapping of the Maine pond against the shore, and the sense of seclusion that comes with being immersed in nature.

title: Underground Hobbit Home in the Deep Forest
subtitle: Custom earth home under 10 acres of Michigan forest
bestFor: Nature lovers and couples seeking solitude
bestSeason: Autumn — the forest's colors are at their most vivid
description: A custom-built hobbit home nestled under the floor of a 10-acre Michigan forest — hand-carved rooms, earthen walls, and a sense of total immersion in the woods. One of the most genuinely unusual places to sleep in the Midwest.
body: As you step into this underground hobbit home, the forest floor above you becomes a ceiling, and the trees' roots stretch down like nature's own cathedral. The hand-carved rooms and earthen walls envelop you in a sense of total immersion in the woods, the scent of damp earth and leaves filling your lungs. We've found that the stillness of the forest is almost palpable here, a quality that seeps into your bones and stays with you long after you've left. The 10-acre forest surrounding you is a world unto itself, full of hidden clearings and secret paths waiting to be uncovered.

title: Wee Nook — A Hobbit Hole
subtitle: Tucked underground in the Tennessee woods
bestFor: Couples seeking a romantic getaway or solo travelers looking for a peaceful retreat
bestSeason: Fall — the surrounding woods are set ablaze with color
description: A 360 sq ft underground hobbit hole in the Tennessee woods — full kitchen, full bathroom, and a door that opens onto the forest floor. Tiny, earthy, and utterly charming. The Shire is real, and it's in Middle Tennessee.
body: As you step into the Wee Nook, a 360 sq ft underground hobbit hole in the Tennessee woods, you're enveloped in a sense of earthy coziness. The full kitchen and bathroom are practical touches, but it's the door that opens onto the forest floor that truly sets this place apart. You can imagine yourself in a scene from a favorite novel, the trees towering above like sentinels. The space is tiny, but it's this compactness that makes it feel so utterly charming, a true retreat from the world above. We've all dreamed of finding our own Shire, and here it is, in the heart of Middle Tennessee.

title: Hobbit Style Underground Cabin
subtitle: Secluded earth home in the Blue Ridge foothills
bestFor: Couples seeking solitude, writers, and nature lovers
bestSeason: Autumn — mild temperatures and foliage season
description: A secluded hobbit-style underground cabin nestled in the valley of Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains. Earth walls, wood beams, and a round door — private, quiet, and shielded by the mountain itself.
body: As you step through the round door of this hobbit-style underground cabin, you'll feel the weight of the Blue Ridge Mountains above you, shielding you from the world. The earth walls and wood beams envelop you in a sense of seclusion, as if the mountain itself has swallowed you whole. The valley stretches out before you, a gentle slope of green that opens up like a canvas, waiting to be explored. We've found that the stillness of this place is a balm for weary souls, a chance to unplug and tune into the rhythms of the natural world.

title: The Hobbit House
subtitle: Fantasy comes home in the Arkansas hills
bestFor: Couples and families seeking a unique, immersive experience
bestSeason: Spring — mild weather and blooming wildflowers
description: A storybook earth home built into the Arkansas hillside with an iconic round door, stone walls, and curved hobbit-scale ceilings. Two bedrooms, whimsical details throughout, and wooded privacy that makes the fantasy feel completely real.
body: As you step through the iconic round door of the Hobbit House, you're enveloped in a world of whimsy and wonder. The earth home's stone walls and curved ceilings seem to grow organically from the Arkansas hillside, as if the very earth itself has been shaped to cradle you in comfort. We find ourselves drawn to the storybook charm of this two-bedroom retreat, where wooded privacy and fantasy details conspire to make the ordinary feel extraordinary. The Hobbit House is a place where the boundaries between reality and fantasy blur, and the beauty of the natural world is always within reach.

title: The Kiva Cave Creek
subtitle: Underground kiva earthen home in the Sonoran desert
bestFor: Couples and solo travelers seeking solitude and a deeper connection with nature
bestSeason: Spring — mild temperatures and wildflower blooms make for ideal desert exploration
description: An underground kiva-inspired earthen home in Cave Creek, AZ — circular, earth-sheltered, and perfectly cool against Arizona's heat. Authentic Native-inspired architecture with handcrafted details, saguaro views, and desert silence.
body: As you step into the Kiva Cave Creek, the desert landscape above gives way to a cool, earth-sheltered space that feels like a natural extension of the Sonoran Desert itself. The circular design of this kiva-inspired earthen home is a nod to authentic Native-inspired architecture, with handcrafted details that add a touch of warmth to the otherwise rugged surroundings. The views of saguaro cacti from the property are a reminder of the unique landscape that Arizona has to offer, and the desert silence is a balm for weary souls. We find ourselves drawn to the simplicity and elegance of this underground dwelling, where the rhythms of nature are the only soundtrack you need.

title: The Caves at Moab — Private Riverside Ranch
subtitle: Red rock caves at a private Colorado River ranch
bestFor: Couples and solo travelers seeking a tranquil, nature-immersed experience
bestSeason: Spring — mild temperatures and wildflower blooms
description: Caves carved directly into the red rock formations of a private riverside ranch outside Moab — surrounded by the canyon country that defines the Southwest. Sleep inside the earth, wake to Arches country light.
body: As you step into the Caves at Moab, you're enveloped by the earthy scent of red rock and the gentle hum of the Colorado River. The cave dwellings, carved directly into the rock formations, offer a unique chance to sleep inside the earth and wake up to the warm, golden light of Arches country. We've found that the best way to experience this place is to rise early, watch the sun creep over the canyon walls, and then spend the day exploring the rugged landscape that defines the Southwest. The private riverside ranch setting provides a sense of seclusion, yet you're still within reach of Moab's amenities and the stunning natural beauty of the surrounding area.

title: The Shire of Montana
subtitle: Fully underground luxury retreat, 55°F year-round
bestFor: Couples and families seeking a unique, secluded retreat
bestSeason: Year-round — constant cool temperature
description: The Shire of Montana is entirely underground — a naturally temperature-stable 55°F retreat built into a Montana hillside. Three bedrooms, full kitchen, luxurious finishes, and the eerie peace of a home that the outside world doesn't know exists.
body: As you step into The Shire of Montana, the world above fades away, and you're enveloped in the eerie peace of a home that's entirely underground. The natural temperature stability of the earth means the air is always a cool 55°F, a welcome respite from the outside world. We find ourselves drawn to the luxurious finishes and full kitchen, where we can prepare meals and gather with loved ones in this unique earth home. The three bedrooms offer ample space to unwind, and the fact that this home is built into a Montana hillside only adds to its allure.

title: The Hobbit Inn
subtitle: Hand-built earth home above the Columbia River
bestFor: Couples seeking solitude, writers, and anyone looking to unplug
bestSeason: Spring — wildflowers bloom in the surrounding hills
description: A curious dwelling built into the hill in a quiet fold of the mountains above the Columbia River in central Washington. Thick earth walls, curved ceilings, and the kind of silence that makes you forget what century it is.
body: As you settle into the Hobbit Inn, the thick earth walls and curved ceilings envelop you in a silence that's both disorienting and calming. The stillness is a palpable thing, a reminder that some landscapes are best experienced without the distractions of the modern world. We've found that the best way to appreciate this unique earth home is to slow down, letting the gentle rhythms of the natural world seep into your bones. The hillside dwelling is a masterclass in understated design, with handbuilt touches that speak to a deep connection with the land.

title: Tiny Houseboat with Portland Harbor Views
subtitle: New England's hippest harbor, from the water
bestFor: Couples seeking a romantic, waterfront getaway
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and lively harbor activity
description: A unique tiny houseboat docked in Portland Harbor, ME — wake to lobster boats and working piers, then walk to the Old Port's celebrated restaurants and galleries. One bedroom, cozy, and utterly unlike any hotel in town.
body: As you step aboard this tiny houseboat, the sounds of Portland Harbor envelop you - the creak of wooden docks, the rumble of lobster boats, and the cries of seagulls. The Old Port's celebrated restaurants and galleries are just a short walk away, but you may find yourself reluctant to leave the cozy confines of your floating home. With its one bedroom and intimate layout, this houseboat is a tranquil retreat from the bustling streets of Portland, offering a unique perspective on the city and its maritime heritage. We love the way the harbor views unfold like a canvas of blues and grays, a constant reminder of the sea's presence.

title: Houseboat NOMAD on Lake Pemaquid
subtitle: Mid-Coast Maine lake life, beautifully unmoored
bestFor: Couples and families seeking a peaceful lake getaway
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and lake swimming season
description: NOMAD is a classic houseboat on Lake Pemaquid in Mid-Coast Maine — a calm, pristine freshwater lake ringed with pine forests. Two bedrooms, a wrap deck, and the quiet confidence of a Maine summer morning on the water.
body: As you step onto the houseboat NOMAD, the gentle lapping of Lake Pemaquid's waters against the hull envelops you in a sense of tranquility. The pine forests that ring this pristine freshwater lake stand tall and still, their scent carried on the morning breeze. We find ourselves drawn to the wrap deck, where the quiet confidence of a Maine summer morning on the water is palpable. Inside, two bedrooms provide cozy retreats, while the houseboat's classic design exudes a sense of understated charm. As the day unfolds, the valley opens up like a theater curtain, revealing a serene landscape that invites exploration and relaxation.

title: Noa's Ark Float-House on the Hudson
subtitle: Artisan floating home on New York's storied river
bestFor: Couples seeking a peaceful getaway
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and long days to enjoy the river views
description: A lovingly crafted float-house moored on the Hudson River at Kingston — two hours from NYC. Artisan wood interiors, river views from every window, and the Catskill Mountains on the horizon. Peaceful, singular, unforgettable.
body: As you step aboard Noa's Ark Float-House, the gentle lapping of the Hudson River against the hull envelops you in a sense of tranquility. With artisan wood interiors and river views from every window, this lovingly crafted float-house feels like a secluded retreat, despite being just two hours from NYC. The Catskill Mountains rise up on the horizon, a constant reminder of the natural beauty that surrounds you. We imagine spending hours watching the river flow by, the play of light on the water, and the stars twinkling to life above.

title: Lake Vermilion Houseboat
subtitle: Untamed Minnesota wilderness, delivered by water
bestFor: Families and groups of friends who love fishing and the outdoors
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and long days perfect for swimming, fishing, and exploring the lake
description: Sleep on Lake Vermilion's wild northern waters aboard a fully equipped houseboat from the Lake Vermilion Houseboat fleet. Three bedrooms, full galley, fishing and kayaks included — immersive Minnesota lake life near the Boundary Waters.
body: As you step aboard the Lake Vermilion Houseboat, the gentle rock of the water and the scent of pine envelop you, drawing you into the rhythms of Minnesota lake life. With three bedrooms and a full galley, this houseboat is equipped for a comfortable stay, whether you're a family or a group of friends. The surrounding waters offer ample opportunities for fishing and kayaking, and the proximity to the Boundary Waters means you can easily explore the region's vast wilderness. As the sun sets, the sky opens up like a canvas of pink and gold, a perfect accompaniment to the sound of lapping water against the hull.

title: Florida Keys Living: Charming Houseboat
subtitle: Island life on the water, Key West style
bestFor: Couples or solo travelers seeking a tranquil, waterfront retreat
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and mostly sunny days
description: A charming houseboat in Key West — the southernmost point in the continental USA. One bedroom, gentle rocking motion, and the sights, sounds, and sunsets of America's most colorful island right outside.
body: As you step onto this charming houseboat in Key West, the gentle rocking motion envelops you, and the sights, sounds, and sunsets of America's most colorful island unfold right outside. With one bedroom, it's an intimate setting, perfect for a couple or solo traveler looking to immerse themselves in the island life. The warm Florida Keys climate means you can enjoy the waterfront views and sounds of the sea year-round, with average temperatures ranging from 79.3°F in May to 84.0°F in July. We find the slower pace of life on the water, combined with the vibrant culture of Key West, makes for a unique and captivating stay.

title: Florida Keys Luxury Houseboat
subtitle: Steps to ocean, reef, and island nightlife
bestFor: Couples and families seeking a relaxing waterfront experience
bestSeason: Winter — mild weather perfect for snorkeling and outdoor activities
description: A fully equipped luxury houseboat at Mile Marker 90 in the upper Florida Keys — prime location steps from restaurants, water sports, and world-class reef snorkeling. Sunrise over the Atlantic, sunset over the Bay.
body: As you step onto this luxury houseboat, the gentle rock of the water beneath your feet sets the tone for a tranquil stay. Located at Mile Marker 90 in the upper Florida Keys, you're surrounded by the soft lapping of waves against the hull and the warm glow of sunrise over the Atlantic. The day unfolds with possibilities: snorkeling in the world-class reefs nearby, trying your hand at water sports, or simply soaking up the sun on the deck. As the day winds down, the sky is set aflame with the colors of sunset over the Bay, a sight to savor from the comfort of your floating home.

title: Kimbo's Kabin — Norris Lake Houseboat
subtitle: Water-access-only float house, pure Tennessee lake life
bestFor: Couples or solo travelers seeking solitude
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and lake swimming season
description: Kimbo's Kabin is a water-access-only houseboat moored on pristine Norris Lake in the Tennessee hill country. Arrive by boat, wake to mirror-flat water, and spend the day swimming off the dock — totally unplugged.
body: As you step onto Kimbo's Kabin, the gentle rock of the houseboat on Norris Lake's calm waters envelops you in a sense of tranquility. We've found that the best way to experience this Tennessee hill country retreat is to fully surrender to its unplugged charm, spending days swimming off the dock and watching the mirror-flat water reflect the surrounding landscape. The fact that it's only accessible by boat adds to the sense of seclusion, making it easy to unplug and unwind. The stillness of the lake in the morning, as the water laps against the hull, is a sound that will stay with you long after you've left.

title: Caddo Lake Houseboat with Kayaks
subtitle: Cypress swamp adventure from your private dock
bestFor: Couples and solo travelers seeking solitude
bestSeason: Spring — wildflowers bloom along the shoreline
description: Float above the hauntingly beautiful waters of Caddo Lake — Texas's only natural lake, draped in Spanish moss and ancient bald cypress. Two bedrooms, kayaks, and a private dock deep in East Texas solitude.
body: As you step onto the Caddo Lake Houseboat, the soft lapping of the water against the hull envelops you, and the Spanish moss-draped cypress trees towering above seem to whisper secrets of the lake. We've found a place where the rhythms of nature still hold sway, where the only sounds are the birds calling and the gentle rocking of the boat. The two bedrooms provide a cozy retreat after a day of exploring the lake's many inlets and waterways, and the kayaks waiting at the private dock beckon you to paddle into the misty dawn or golden sunset.

title: Casa Ocaso Houseboat on Lake Travis
subtitle: 42-foot Gibson houseboat, rooftop sunset deck
bestFor: Couples seeking a romantic getaway
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and long days perfect for lake activities
description: A 42-foot Gibson houseboat moored on Lake Travis with a rooftop lounge made for Hill Country sunsets. One bedroom below, the whole lake above — 30 minutes from downtown Austin.
body: As you step onto the Casa Ocaso Houseboat, the gentle lapping of Lake Travis' waters against the hull sets the tone for a tranquil retreat. The 42-foot Gibson houseboat is moored in a secluded spot, offering an unobstructed view of the Texas Hill Country sunsets from its rooftop lounge. Below deck, a cozy bedroom provides a peaceful refuge, while the lake's vast expanse stretches out above, waiting to be explored. We're just 30 minutes from downtown Austin, but the city feels a world away as you watch the stars twinkle to life above.

title: Portland Floating Home with Sauna
subtitle: Steam, soak, and float on the Columbia
bestFor: Couples seeking a relaxing getaway
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather for kayaking and outdoor exploration
description: A Pacific Northwest floating home near the Columbia River with a private sauna — the ultimate after-adventure recovery retreat. Kayak from your doorstep, then unwind with the river rocking you to sleep.
body: As you step into this Portland floating home, the gentle rocking of the water beneath you sets the tone for a tranquil retreat. With a private sauna to unwind in, you can soothe your muscles after a day of kayaking or exploring the city. The Columbia River flows softly outside, a constant reminder of the natural world just beyond your doorstep. We imagine you'll spend your evenings drifting off to sleep to the sound of the river, the city lights of Portland twinkling in the distance.

title: Floating House on Flathead Lake
subtitle: Rooftop kayaks on Montana's crown jewel lake
bestFor: Couples or families seeking a serene lake experience
bestSeason: Summer — ideal for swimming, kayaking, and warm weather
description: A genuine floating house moored on Flathead Lake — Montana's 30-mile inland sea beneath the Mission Mountains. Three bedrooms, rooftop sun deck, kayaks, and silence broken only by the water lapping below.
body: As you step onto this floating house, the gentle lapping of the water against the hull envelops you, a soothing melody that sets the tone for a tranquil stay. Moored on Flathead Lake, beneath the majestic Mission Mountains, this three-bedroom houseboat offers a unique perspective on the surroundings, with a rooftop sun deck that invites you to soak in the vast expanse of Montana's 30-mile inland sea. The silence is almost palpable, broken only by the occasional sound of water or the calls of birds, creating an atmosphere that's both calming and invigorating.

title: Little Lux Floating Home
subtitle: SF Bay views from your private floating dock
bestFor: Couples seeking a romantic waterfront getaway
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and calm bay waters
description: One of Sausalito's celebrated floating homes — a luminous one-bedroom retreat on Richardson Bay with sweeping San Francisco skyline views. Bobbing gently on the water with the Golden Gate minutes away.
body: As you step into the Little Lux Floating Home, the gentle bobbing of the water beneath your feet is a reminder that you're not on solid ground. The one-bedroom retreat is a tranquil oasis on Richardson Bay, with the San Francisco skyline unfolding like a canvas of steel and stone before your eyes. We've found that the best way to experience this floating home is to settle into its rhythms, watching the light dance across the water as the Golden Gate Bridge rises up in the distance. The proximity to the iconic landmark is a bonus, but it's the sense of being suspended between land and sea that makes this stay truly unique.

title: Gorgeous Floating Home at Skyline Moorage
subtitle: Brand-new floating home on the Willamette
bestFor: Couples or small groups looking for a relaxing, waterfront stay with easy access to Portland's amenities
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and long days make it ideal for exploring the city and enjoying the private deck
description: Brand-new floating home at Portland's Skyline Moorage on the lower Willamette River. Two bedrooms, full kitchen, and a private deck right above the water — downtown Portland a short drive away.
body: As you step into this brand-new floating home at Skyline Moorage, the gentle lapping of the Willamette River against the hull sets the tone for a tranquil urban retreat. With two bedrooms and a full kitchen, you'll have everything you need to settle in and make the most of your time in Portland. The private deck, suspended just above the water, offers a unique perspective on the city - watch the sun set over the river, or enjoy a morning coffee as the mist rises from the surface. Downtown Portland is just a short drive away, making it easy to explore the city's renowned food scene, breweries, and cultural attractions.

title: Postcard Cabins Lake Hartwell
subtitle: Tiny lakeside cabin in South Carolina Upcountry
bestFor: Couples and solo travelers seeking a peaceful lake retreat
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather perfect for lake swimming and kayaking
description: Postcard Cabins on the shores of Lake Hartwell in South Carolina's scenic Upcountry — 40 upscale tiny cabins 50 minutes from Greenville. Kayaking, swimming, and the unhurried quiet of a lake community outside your door.
body: As you step into one of the 40 tiny cabins at Postcard Cabins, the shores of Lake Hartwell unfold before you like a serene canvas. We're drawn to the unhurried quiet of this lake community, where kayaking and swimming are just a few steps from your door. The cabins themselves are upscale and intimate, providing a cozy retreat from the world. With Greenville just 50 minutes away, you can easily balance lake time with city explorations, making this stay a unique blend of relaxation and adventure.

title: Postcard Cabins Dale Hollow
subtitle: Tiny cabin community on Tennessee's clearest lake
bestFor: Couples and families with dogs, looking for a peaceful retreat from the city
bestSeason: Summer - lake swimming season, when the water is warm and the days are long
description: Postcard Cabins at Dale Hollow — 40 premium tiny cabins on hundreds of private acres in Celina, Tennessee, just 2 hours from Nashville. Dale Hollow Lake is one of the clearest in the country and the swimming is extraordinary.
body: As you step into one of the 40 tiny cabins at Postcard Cabins Dale Hollow, you're immediately immersed in a world where design and nature converge. The cabins themselves are sleek and modern, with a kitchenette, dining table, and a queen bed or bunk bed that can accommodate 2-4 guests. But it's the surroundings that truly make this stay special - hundreds of private acres that slope down to the shores of Dale Hollow Lake, one of the clearest lakes in the country. The swimming is extraordinary, and the scenery is equally impressive, with a valley that opens up like a theater curtain to reveal the lake's glassy surface. bestFor: Couples or solo travelers looking for a peaceful retreat
bestSeason: Spring — wildflowers are in bloom
description: As seen on HGTV! "My Tiny Cabin" is a complete house in just 288 square feet, built as an experiment in simplification. Situated under oak trees on a 1.5-acre working neighborhood mini-farm in Austin.
body: As you step into this tiny cabin, you're immersed in an experiment in simplification, where every detail has been carefully considered to create a sense of warmth and comfort. The 288 square feet of space are thoughtfully designed, with the gentle shade of oak trees overhead and the soothing sounds of a 1.5-acre working mini-farm all around. We've had the chance to explore this unique stay, featured on HGTV, and it's clear that the emphasis is on slowing down and appreciating the simple things. The cabin's compact size belies a sense of expansiveness, with the surrounding landscape unfolding like a canvas of rolling hills and wildflowers.

title: Osprey Treehouse — Columbia River Gorge
subtitle: Built around a 42-inch Douglas Fir
editorNote: Suspend yourself in the Pacific Northwest canopy at this intimate treehouse retreat.
bestFor: Couples seeking solitude
bestSeason: Fall — the canopy turns gold
description: A 20-foot octagon treehouse built around a 42-inch old-growth Douglas Fir. Oversized windows and a sliding door give you the feeling of being suspended in the Pacific Northwest canopy. Sleeps 2 adults.
body: As you arrive at the Osprey Treehouse, the canopy of the Pacific Northwest forest envelops you, and the scent of old-growth Douglas Fir fills the air. The 20-foot octagon treehouse, built around a 42-inch trunk, seems to grow organically from the forest floor. Inside, oversized windows and a sliding door dissolve the boundaries between you and the forest, giving you the sensation of being suspended among the trees. At night, the darkness is almost palpable, and the sounds of the forest provide a soothing background hum. The treehouse sleeps two adults, making it an intimate retreat for couples seeking solitude.
areaGuide: The Columbia River Gorge stretches out before you, a valley that opens up like a theater curtain. The town of Stevenson, Washington, is nearby, with its quaint shops and restaurants. Visitors should know that the area is prone to rain, so it's essential to pack accordingly. The gorge offers plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities, such as hiking and kayaking, and the scenic vistas are breathtaking.

faqs.question: How do I get to the Osprey Treehouse?
faqs.answer: The treehouse is located in Stevenson, Washington, and can be reached by car. The exact address will be provided after booking.

faqs.question: What should I bring?
faqs.answer: Pack layers for rain and cooler temperatures, as well as comfortable shoes for exploring the forest.

faqs.question: What activities are nearby?
faqs.answer: The Columbia River Gorge offers hiking, kayaking, and scenic vistas. The town of Stevenson also has shops and restaurants to explore.

faqs.question: Are there any seasonal considerations?
faqs.answer: The area is prone to rain, so it's essential to pack accordingly. The treehouse is available year-round, but the forest is particularly beautiful during the fall season.

title: Smoky Mountain Bubble Dome

At dusk, the private hot tub beckons, a spot to soak under a canopy of fireflies as the stars begin to twinkle. We've found that the stillness of this secluded spot is a balm for weary souls, a chance to slow down and tune into the rhythms of nature.

The A-frame's cozy interior and the gentle gurgle of the creek outside conspire to lull you into a state of deep relaxation, making it the perfect haven to unwind after a day of adventure.

editorNote: A private lighthouse on the Maine coast, where the rhythms of the sea set the tone for a tranquil retreat.
bestFor: Families and groups seeking a unique and historic coastal experience
bestSeason: Summer — warm weather and long days perfect for outdoor activities
description: A private lighthouse property on Chauncey Creek with a full dock, kayaks, and direct water access. Five bedrooms, stunning tidal views, and the quintessential Maine coastal experience. Perfect for family reunions or group retreats.
body: As you arrive at the private lighthouse on Chauncey Creek, the tidal views unfold like a canvas of blues and greens. The five bedrooms and full dock create a sense of expansive freedom, perfect for family reunions or group retreats. We spend our days kayaking through the creek, exploring the Maine coast's hidden coves and inlets, and our nights gathered around the water's edge, watching the stars reflected in the calm waters. The lighthouse itself stands as a testament to the region's rich history, its presence a reminder of the countless stories that have unfolded on these shores.
areaGuide: Kittery, Maine, is a treasure trove of coastal charm, with its quaint shops, seafood restaurants, and historic landmarks. Visitors can explore the nearby Fort Foster Park, with its scenic trails and picnic areas, or take a short drive to the picturesque town of Portsmouth, New Hampshire. The area is also renowned for its fresh seafood, with lobster rolls and fish markets aplenty.

faqs.question: What is the best way to get to the lighthouse?
faqs.answer: The lighthouse is accessible by car, with parking available on site. Alternatively, visitors can fly into Portland International Jetport and take a taxi or rental car to Kittery.

faqs.question: What activities are available in the area?
faqs.answer: The area offers a range of activities, including kayaking, hiking, and fishing. Visitors can also explore the nearby towns and cities, such as Portsmouth and Kennebunkport.

faqs.question: What should I bring?
faqs.answer: Visitors should bring comfortable clothing, layers for cooler evenings, and sturdy shoes for outdoor activities. Don't forget to pack a camera to capture the stunning views and wildlife.

bestFor: Couples or solo travelers seeking a unique, immersive experience in a maritime setting

description: A charming tiny houseboat moored in Portland Harbor with stunning views of the working waterfront. Fall asleep to the gentle rocking of the tide and wake to lobster boats heading out at dawn. A one-of-a-kind Maine experience.

The harbor views are a constant presence, a reminder of the unique perspective this floating home offers. Inside, the cozy space is designed to make the most of its compact footprint, with clever touches that make you feel like you're getting away with something special. At dawn, the lobster boats head out, their quiet chatter and diesel engines a reminder that this is a working harbor, and you're a part of it, if only for a little while. As night falls, the stars reflect off the water, and the city lights twinkle like a distant constellation. We find ourselves slowing down, letting the rhythm of the tide dictate our pace, and watching the world go by from the comfort of our little houseboat. The experience is quintessentially Maine, a chance to immerse yourself in the state's maritime culture and traditions.
areaGuide: Portland's waterfront is a thriving, eclectic mix of old and new, with converted warehouses, trendy restaurants, and boutiques. The city's renowned food scene is within walking distance, with plenty of opportunities to sample the freshest seafood, craft beers, and local specialties. Visitors can explore the nearby Portland Head Light, one of the most iconic lighthouses on the East Coast, or take a stroll along the Eastern Promenade, which offers stunning views of the harbor and the city.

faqs.answer: Yes, the Portland area offers a wide range of activities, including sailing, kayaking, and fishing. Guests can also explore the city's many museums, galleries, and historic sites.

faqs.answer: The houseboat is available for booking from spring to fall, with the peak season being summer. Guests should be aware that the harbor can be quiet and peaceful during the off-season, but some amenities and services may be limited.

title: Stargazing Bliss in Dome with Sauna & Hot Tub
subtitle: Sleep under a billion stars near Zion
editorNote: Sleep under the stars in a futuristic geodesic dome, surrounded by the serene landscapes of the American Southwest.
bestFor: Couples and solo travelers seeking solitude and stargazing opportunities
bestSeason: Fall — the desert landscape takes on a warm, golden light, and the nights are cool and clear for stargazing
description: A brand-new geodesic dome nestled in the serene landscapes of Glendale, Utah. Panoramic views of the surrounding desert, a private sauna, and a hot tub under the stars. One of the darkest skies in the American Southwest.
body: As you arrive at this geodesic dome in Glendale, Utah, the vast expanse of the desert landscape unfolds before you. The dome's sleek, modern design seems to blend seamlessly into the surroundings, as if it's been plucked from the future and dropped into this serene wilderness. Inside, the space is cozy and intimate, with large windows that frame the panoramic views of the desert, inviting the outdoors in. At night, the dome transforms into a stargazing haven, with some of the darkest skies in the American Southwest offering an unparalleled celestial show. The private sauna and hot tub are the perfect accompaniments to a night of stargazing, allowing you to soak under the stars and feel the vastness of the universe. The stillness of the desert night is almost palpable, punctuated only by the occasional hoot of an owl or the distant howl of a coyote.
areaGuide: Glendale, Utah, is a tranquil desert town surrounded by the rugged beauty of the American Southwest. The nearby Zion National Park is a must-visit, with its towering sandstone cliffs and narrow canyons carved by the Virgin River. The park's unique rock formations and diverse wildlife make it a hiker's paradise, with trails ranging from easy strolls to more challenging climbs. For a taste of local culture, head to the nearby town of Orderville, where you can find quaint shops, restaurants, and galleries showcasing the work of local artists.

faqs.question: How do I get to the dome?
faqs.answer: The dome is located in Glendale, Utah, and can be reached by car. The nearest airport is in St. George, Utah, about an hour's drive away. You can also rent a car or take a shuttle from the airport to the dome.

faqs.question: What should I bring?
faqs.answer: Be sure to pack comfortable clothing, sturdy shoes, and layers for cooler evenings. Don't forget your binoculars for stargazing and a camera to capture the stunning desert landscapes.

faqs.question: What activities are nearby?
faqs.answer: Zion National Park is just a short drive away, offering hiking, canyoneering, and rock climbing. You can also explore the nearby town of Orderville, visit the Zion Human History Museum, or take a scenic drive through the desert landscapes.

faqs.question: Are there any seasonal considerations?
faqs.answer: The desert climate can be hot during the summer months, so be sure to stay hydrated and plan your activities accordingly. Winter months can be cool, so pack warm clothing and enjoy the stars on clearer nights.

title: Point Robinson Lighthouse — Keeper's Quarters

bestFor: Couples and solo travelers looking for a unique, historic experience
bestSeason: Spring and Fall — mild weather and prime whale watching season
description: A restored lighthouse keeper's quarters on Vashon Island — accessible only by ferry. Restored to capture the historic character of the original building. Stunning Puget Sound views and whale watching opportunities.
body: As you step into the Point Robinson Lighthouse Keeper's Quarters, the creak of the old wooden floorboards beneath your feet is a reminder that you're walking in the footsteps of those who once tended the light that guided mariners through the Puget Sound. The quarters have been restored to capture the historic character of the original building, and the attention to detail is evident in every nook and cranny. From the keeper's quarters, you can gaze out at the stunning views of the Puget Sound, where the sea meets the sky and the Olympic Mountains rise up in the distance. On a clear day, you might even catch a glimpse of whales breaching in the distance, their massive forms undulating through the water.

body: As you step into The Big Buffalo, the worn wooden floors and original water closet transport you to a bygone era. This 1894 historic hotel, once the Capitol Hotel, now comprises three connected apartments on Buffalo's Main Street, its Old West character still palpable throughout. The back staircase, built for 'Ladies of the Night', whispers stories of the past, while the pool on premises offers a serene retreat from the town's bustle. We imagine ourselves wandering the halls, tracing the history that seeps from every brick and beam.

Built in 1884 as the first fully African American fire company in Washington DC, the space has been meticulously renovated by a world-famous interior designer. The result is a 3,000 sq ft haven with 5 bedrooms and 4 bathrooms, perfect for groups looking to experience the city in style. The exposed architecture and high ceilings give the space an airy feel, while the carefully chosen decor adds a touch of sophistication. You can almost hear the echoes of the past as you walk through the rooms, the creaks of the old wooden floors a reminder of the stories these walls could tell.

Washington Convention Center is also within walking distance, and the Capital One Arena is just a short drive away. The area is also home to a variety of restaurants and bars, offering everything from traditional Southern cuisine to modern fusion dishes.

faqs.question: Is the loft suitable for groups?
faqs.answer: Yes, the loft is perfect for groups, with 5 bedrooms and 4 bathrooms. It's a great space for families, friends, or colleagues looking to experience the city together.

title: Pelican Bay Lighthouse
subtitle: A privately owned, working lighthouse on the Oregon Coast
editorNote: Stay in a working lighthouse with captivating Pacific Ocean views
bestFor: Couples seeking a unique and romantic getaway
bestSeason: Summer — the warmest weather and longest days
description: A privately owned, working lighthouse perched over Brookings, OR with captivating Pacific Ocean views. The Keeper's Suite is lofted on the upper floor. A legacy family home brimming with warmth and coastal charm.
body: As you approach the Pelican Bay Lighthouse, the sound of the Pacific Ocean grows louder, and the salty air fills your lungs. You're about to step into a legacy family home that's been perched over Brookings, Oregon, for years, its warmth and coastal charm waiting to envelop you. The Keeper's Suite, lofted on the upper floor, is your private retreat, with captivating Pacific Ocean views that seem to shift with every passing moment. The lighthouse itself is a working one, a testament to the area's rich maritime history, and its presence is a reminder that you're in a place where the sea has always been a part of everyday life. As you settle in, the rhythms of the coast will start to seep into your bones - the way the light changes, the sound of the gulls, the smell of the ocean. It's a place to slow down, to watch the world go by from a unique vantage point. We find ourselves drawn to the upper floor, where the Keeper's Suite beckons, its lofted ceilings and cozy nooks the perfect place to curl up with a book or simply watch the sea.
areaGuide: The Pelican Bay Lighthouse is just a short walk from Sporthaven Beach, where you can spend hours exploring the tide pools and watching the surfers. The Port of Brookings Harbor is also within walking distance, with its bustling marina and seafood restaurants. If you're looking to explore further afield, Crescent City, California, is just a short drive away, with its own charming downtown area and scenic coastal views. The area is also home to a number of natural attractions, including the Rogue River and the Siskiyou Mountains, making it a great base for outdoor enthusiasts.

faqs.question: How do I get to the Pelican Bay Lighthouse?

faqs.question: What should I bring with me?

faqs.question: What are some nearby activities?

title: Wander Friday Harbor
subtitle: Island escape accessible by ferry or floatplane
location: Friday Harbor, San Juan Island, Washington
editorNote: Wake up to the sound of the ocean and spend your days exploring the wild beauty of San Juan Island from this luxurious waterfront escape.
bestFor: Couples and families seeking a tranquil and luxurious island getaway
bestSeason: Summer — the warmest weather and longest days make it ideal for outdoor exploration
description: San Juan Island is accessible only by ferry or floatplane — and this Wander property sits at the heart of it. Watch orca whales from the deck, explore the island by bike, and work remotely with Starlink WiFi.
body: As you step off the ferry and onto San Juan Island, the rhythm of the ocean and the calls of seagulls envelop you, setting the tone for a tranquil stay at Wander Friday Harbor. This luxurious waterfront escape is a masterclass in understated elegance, with a private haven that wakes you to the soothing sounds of the ocean and a rejuvenating sauna to melt away stress after a day of exploration. The deck is the perfect spot to watch orca whales glide through the Puget Sound, their sleek forms a reminder of the wild beauty that surrounds you. As the sun sets, gather around the crackling fire pit, sharing stories and creating lasting memories under the starlit sky. The hot tub, perched to take in the captivating ocean views, is the ultimate spot to unwind and let the beauty of the Pacific Northwest seep into your soul.
areaGuide: Friday Harbor, the charming town at the heart of San Juan Island, is a short stroll away, offering a mix of boutique shops, art galleries, and restaurants serving fresh seafood. The island itself is a haven for outdoor enthusiasts, with miles of scenic bike trails, kayaking routes, and whale-watching tours. Be sure to explore the nearby American Camp and English Camp, historic sites that tell the story of the island's rich cultural heritage. As you wander through the island's picturesque landscapes, keep an eye out for the diverse wildlife, including bald eagles, seals, and sea lions.

faqs.question: How do I get to Wander Friday Harbor?
faqs.answer: The property is accessible by ferry or floatplane, and we recommend checking the schedule in advance to plan your trip. Once you arrive, the property is a short drive or bike ride from the town of Friday Harbor.

faqs.question: What should I bring?
faqs.answer: We recommend packing layers for your stay, as the Pacific Northwest weather can be cool and rainy, even in the summer. You may also want to bring binoculars for whale-watching and a camera to capture the stunning views.

faqs.question: What activities are nearby?
faqs.answer: The property is perfectly situated for outdoor enthusiasts, with bike trails, kayaking routes, and whale-watching tours all within easy reach. You can also explore the town of Friday Harbor, visit the nearby historic sites, or simply relax on the deck and take in the views.

faqs.question: Are there any seasonal considerations?
faqs.answer: Yes, the best time to see orca whales is from May to October, and the summer months are the busiest time on the island. If you're looking for a more peaceful stay, consider visiting in the spring or fall, when the weather is still mild and the crowds are smaller.
